reviewed_by: Codex: AI-assisted separate bounded visual edition pass, not independent specialist certification
editorial_policy: AI-assisted normalized working capture of Montgomery’s printed Hebrew-letter editions, visually compared with the held page images; partial source-page review, not a diplomatic text, full character collation, translation or specialist certification. Printed inscription line numbers retained; implicit opening line 1 supplied by the project. Physical page wrapping, word spacing and most typographic punctuation normalized. Printed square brackets remain source restorations, including cross-line restorations; ... normalizes source loss runs without asserting a lost-letter count. ⟦word?⟧ marks project capture doubt, distinct from a source restoration. Source inferior dots, Syriac upper diacritics/seyame, pointing, precise final-letter shapes and source punctuation are NOT exhaustively encoded or collated; the unchanged facsimiles control those details. Recognized Mandaic marked dalet is encoded as ד̄ (dalet plus U+0304), but exhaustive mark placement and consonants remain open. English captions, erasure/elided/sic annotations and Exterior are source editorial matter, not words of the incantation; an em dash explicitly separates a normalized editorial annotation. No.11 retains an apparently unpaired source bracket inside a marked project doubt without inventing its closing boundary. No readings supplied from neighboring witnesses or grammar. Nos.31–37 are source-classified Syriac and nos.38–40 Mandaic; the stored Hebrew-letter texts are TRANSLITERATIONS, not native Syriac/Mandaic-script recoveries. Montgomery explains this convention at printed p.11 / PDF p.17; original-script facsimile recovery remains separate. No public-release or personal-audit completion decision. Separate subsequent source pass over all forty main Montgomery blocks (AIT27 printed1–11 only). Source repetition preserved, including No34 line14 repeated בת. Project doubts use double brackets, not scholarly restoration notation. No claim of full character/dot collation or native Syriac/Mandaic recovery.
